definitions.gloss: pickup; going to meet someone; welcoming a guest
definitions.explanation: The act of going to meet or pick someone up — most often a child from daycare/school, or a guest arriving from elsewhere. Polite form of {迎|むか}え with the honorific お-.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}のお{迎|むか}えに{行|い}く。
examples.english: I'm going to pick up the kids.

examples.japanese: {駅|えき}までお{迎|むか}えに{参|まい}ります。
examples.english: I will come to meet you at the station.

examples.japanese: {保育園|ほいくえん}のお{迎|むか}えの{時間|じかん}に{遅|おく}れないように{気|き}をつけている。
examples.english: I make sure not to be late for the daycare pickup time.

notes:
Polite noun form of the verb {迎|むか}える (to meet, to welcome). The opposite of {見送|みおく}り (seeing someone off).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{迎|むか}えに{行|い}く: to go to meet/pick up
- お{迎|むか}えに{来|く}る: to come to meet/pick up
- お{迎|むか}えの{時間|じかん}: pickup time
- お{迎|むか}えの{車|くるま}: pickup car
- {空港|くうこう}のお{迎|むか}え: airport pickup

USAGE: Standard daily-life vocabulary, especially for parents with children in daycare. Polite enough for business contexts when offering to meet a guest at a station or airport.

EUPHEMISTIC USE: お{迎|むか}えが{来|く}る ('the one who comes to meet has come') is a softened way to refer to death — typically pictured as a Buddhist or divine figure coming to escort the deceased.
